The series “Studies in Big Data” (SBD) publishes new developments and advances in 
the various areas of Big Data- quickly and with a high quality. The intent is to cover the 
theory, research, development, and applications of Big Data, as embedded in the ﬁelds 
of engineering, computer science, physics, economics and life sciences. The books of 
the series refer to the analysis and understanding of large, complex, and/or distributed 
data sets generated from recent digital sources coming from sensors or other physical 
instruments as well as simulations, crowd sourcing, social networks or other internet 
transactions, such as emails or video click streams and other. The series contains 
monographs, lecture notes and edited volumes in Big Data spanning the areas of 
computational intelligence including neural networks, evolutionary computation, 
soft computing, fuzzy systems, as well as artiﬁcial intelligence, data mining, modern 
statistics and Operations research, as well as self-organizing systems. Of particular 
value to both the contributors and the readership are the short publication timeframe 
and the world-wide distribution, which enable both wide and rapid dissemination of 
research output. 
The books of this series are reviewed in a single blind peer review process. 
Indexed by SCOPUS, EI Compendex, SCIMAGO and zbMA TH. 
All books published in the series are submitted for consideration in Web of Science.

Foreword 
The authors of this thought-provoking book skillfully explore the evolution of 
libraries in the digital age, demonstrating how the fusion of Internet and AI technolo-
gies has revolutionized the accessibility and processing of information. Through their 
extensive professional expertise, they navigate the challenges libraries now encounter 
and emphasize the necessity for these institutions to evolve in order to maintain their 
crucial role in education and research. 
Presenting a compelling narrative of libraries adapting to societal shifts, the 
authors paint a vivid picture of a modern library that seamlessly integrates advanced 
technologies to deliver up-to-date knowledge efﬁciently. Their foresight in lever-
aging AI tools not only showcases the potential for streamlining data analysis but 
also underscores the irreplaceable role of human creativity in shaping the future of 
information management. Obviously, along with the professional role of libraries, 
there is also a social role and task that is undergoing a total transformation in the age 
of mobile communication. 
IN and WITH this insightful book, the authors offer a glimpse into a future where 
AI complements human efforts, shedding light on the symbiotic relationship between 
technology and human ingenuity in shaping the libraries of tomorrow. 
Hagen, Germany 
June 2024 
Herwig Unger
v

Preface 
Libraries, enduring bastions of knowledge, learning, and community, are at a pivotal 
juncture today. The digital revolution has propelled them into a transformative 
phase, necessitating swift adaptation to new technologies while preserving their 
foundational identity and values. This book chronicles libraries’ journey through 
an increasingly digital, data-driven, and disruptive landscape, highlighting their 
remarkable resilience and capacity to evolve, even as they redeﬁne the essence of 
modern libraries. This resilience reassures library leaders and stakeholders, instilling 
conﬁdence in libraries’ ability to navigate this digital transformation. 
Libraries are undergoing not only evolution but also profound transformation. 
Once characterized primarily by physical collections and transactions, they have 
evolved into dynamic spaces for creation, collaboration, and community engage-
ment. There has been a shift from consumption to creation, from a focus on hold-
ings to enhancing access, and, importantly, from a library-centric to a user-centric 
approach. This shift ensures that libraries tailor services to meet user needs and pref-
erences, making users feel considered and valued. The emergence of digital media, 
automation, artiﬁcial intelligence, and big data accelerates these changes. 
This book represents more than a collection of ideas; it synthesizes cross-
disciplinary research, expert interviews, and direct involvement in innovative library 
projects. It offers a comprehensive perspective on the multidimensional transforma-
tion unfolding in libraries, transcending historical shifts. The “conceptual framework 
and roadmap” presented here provides a structured approach for libraries to under-
stand and implement digital transformation. It encompasses foundational principles, 
strategic insights, and actionable steps for harnessing emerging technologies while 
upholding core values. Moreover, the book showcases pioneering initiatives that 
glimpse potential digital futures. 
A central theme explored is the delicate balance between continuity and change, 
underscored by libraries’ ongoing evolution. The COVID-19 pandemic has ampli-
ﬁed digital trends and highlighted libraries’ role as inclusive community spaces, 
hubs for digital literacy, creative centers, and arenas for civic engagement. However, 
persistent economic constraints and rapid technological advancements pose ongoing 
challenges. It is crucial to engage in strategic planning to sustain public funding and
vii

viii Preface
demonstrate the enduring value libraries offer as both physical sanctuaries and virtual 
platforms for community interaction. This emphasis on strategic planning will make 
the audience feel prepared and proactive in facing challenges. 
This book offers a nuanced perspective on the digital transformation of libraries. 
While acknowledging the undeniable beneﬁts, such as enhanced access and improved 
services, it also addresses associated risks if changes outpace institutional capaci-
ties or need to align with community needs. These risks include digital exclusion, 
privacy concerns, and the potential for technology to substitute human interaction. 
Rather than adopting new technologies uncritically, the book advocates for a user-
centered strategy where digital platforms serve as tools rather than solutions. It 
encourages deliberate experimentation and evidence-based integration of emerging 
systems, ensuring that changes serve genuine user needs rather than merely chasing 
technological novelty. 
We hope this book assists libraries in effectively leveraging technology to enhance 
access, inclusion, discovery, and community engagement. While acknowledging the 
profound digital potential, it emphasizes the importance of channeling it construc-
tively to avoid disparities and disruptions to traditional library roles. Grounded in 
practical analysis and real-world experiences, the insights and advice offered here 
are invaluable to library leaders and stakeholders navigating complex strategic deci-
sions and grappling with digital challenges. This practical guidance aims to equip 
them with the tools and knowledge necessary to navigate the digital transformation 
of libraries successfully. 
Bangkok, Thailand 
June 2024 
Phayung Meesad 
Anirach Mingkhawn

Part I 
Historical and Conceptual Foundations 
Part I offers a comprehensive exploration of the evolution of libraries, tracing their 
transformation from ancient scroll repositories to modern digital archives. Initially, 
libraries emerged as static custodians of knowledge in early civilizations such as 
Mesopotamia, Egypt, and Syria, where they preserved sacred and scholarly texts. 
These early institutions laid the groundwork for the Library of Alexandria, founded 
in the third century BCE. Renowned for its vast collections and the patronage of 
scholars worldwide, the Library of Alexandria was pivotal in developing libraries. 
It amassed an extensive collection of scrolls and introduced the concept of a public 
library open to all who sought knowledge, setting a signiﬁcant precedent for future 
libraries. 
The narrative then transitions to the ﬁfteenth century, when Johannes Gutenberg 
marked the revolutionary advent of the printing press. This innovation democratized 
access to books, signiﬁcantly altering the landscape of libraries. The printing press 
enabled the rapid dissemination of knowledge, paving the way for broader public 
education and literacy. 
Subsequent sections examine the profound impact of twentieth- and twenty-ﬁrst-
century technological advancements, including the advent of computers, the Internet, 
and digitalization. These developments have transformed libraries into dynamic hubs 
that store information, provide extensive digital services, and access global informa-
tion networks. This evolution has fundamentally changed the roles of librarians and 
the expectations of library users. 
The discussion then delves into libraries’ challenges and opportunities in the 
digital era. As libraries transition into digital spaces, they face digital preservation 
and technological obsolescence issues. Obsolescence refers to a condition where 
technologies or formats become outdated or useless, often due to the advent of 
newer alternatives. Libraries now grapple with the challenge of preserving digital 
content, which can rapidly become inaccessible due to technological changes, and 
managing the swift pace of technological progress that may render current formats 
obsolete. Moreover, there is a growing imperative for libraries to act as community 
technology centers, supporting digital access and literacy. Libraries are increasingly 
transforming into comprehensive community centers, providing technology access

2 Part I: Historical and Conceptual Foundations
and digital literacy education, thereby contributing to a more interconnected and 
knowledgeable society. 
These transformations underscore the critical role libraries will continue to 
play as portals for accessing knowledge and cultural resources. As centers that 
enhance digital literacy, provide technological tools, and foster continuous learning 
and community interaction, libraries adapt to meet their users’ evolving needs. 
This ongoing progression suggests that libraries will remain integral to societal 
development, continually shaped by technological and social advancements.

Chapter 1 
Evolving Libraries: From Ancient Scrolls 
to Digital Archives 
Figure 1.1 illustrates the transformation of libraries from ancient to medieval monastic times. 
On the left, it depicts an ancient library ﬁlled with scrolls and architectural grandeur, show-
casing intricate columns and statues, signifying the rich cultural heritage and scholarly 
activities of the era. Scholars are seen engrossed in reading and transcribing texts. On the 
right, a medieval monastic library is presented, characterized by wooden shelves lined with 
bound books and illuminated by natural light streaming through arched windows. Monks 
are engaged in quiet study and manuscript copying, reﬂecting the monastic dedication to 
preserving knowledge during the Middle Ages. 
1.1 Introduction to the Evolution of Libraries 
Throughout history, libraries have not just transformed but have been instrumental 
in shaping societies. They started as exclusive repositories of clay tablets and scrolls 
in ancient times. They have now evolved into modern public institutions that lever-
age digital technologies to cater to diverse community needs. This chapter takes a 
deep dive into the evolution of libraries, tracking their journey from the ancient world 
through the Middle Ages and Renaissance. It also explores the rise of public libraries 
in the 19th century, the inﬂuence of technology in the 20th century, and the digi-
tal revolution of the 21st century. The chapter underscores the inspiring resilience 
of libraries and how they have ﬂexibly adapted to changing societal needs while 
upholding their core mission of preserving knowledge. For instance, the Library of 
Alexandria in ancient Egypt, established in the 3rd century BCE, aimed to gather 
all the world’s knowledge and became a hub of intellectual activity. This unwaver-
ing commitment to preserving knowledge has not just earned libraries our respect 
and admiration but has also played a pivotal role in the progress of civilizations, 
such as the Renaissance period, where libraries were crucial in the dissemination of 
knowledge, and the Enlightenment era, where they were instrumental in fostering 
intellectual discourse [ 68].
