430 Glossary 
Algorithmic Bias The potential for AI algorithms to produce unfair or discrimina-
tory outcomes in library services due to inherent biases in their design or training 
data. 
Algorithmic Technologies The use of complex computational procedures in library 
systems for tasks such as information retrieval, recommendation systems, and data 
analysis. 
Algorithmic Transparency The practice of making the decision-making processes 
of AI algorithms used in libraries open and understandable to users and stakeholders. 
Ancient Libraries Historical institutions that collected and preserved knowledge 
in early civilizations, such as the Library of Alexandria, serving as precursors to 
modern libraries. 
Artiﬁcial Intelligence The simulation of human intelligence in machines, used in 
libraries to automate tasks, enhance services, and improve user experiences. 
Assistive Technologies Tools and devices that help individuals with disabilities 
access library resources and services, such as screen readers, magniﬁcation software, 
and adaptive keyboards. 
Augmented Reality Technology that overlays digital information onto the physical 
world, used in libraries to enhance user experiences and provide interactive learning 
opportunities. 
Automated Cataloging The use of AI and machine learning to automatically clas-
sify, tag, and organize library materials, improving efﬁciency and accuracy in cata-
loging processes. 
Automation The use of technology to perform tasks with minimal human inter-
vention, applied in libraries to streamline processes such as circulation, inventory 
management, and data entry. 
Artiﬁcial Intelligence (AI) The simulation of human intelligence processes by 
machines, especially computer systems. 
Augmented Reality (AR) An interactive experience of a real-world environment 
where objects in the real world are enhanced by computer-generated perceptual 
information. 
Anonymization The process of removing personally identiﬁable information from 
data sets so that the people whom the data describes remain anonymous. 
Artiﬁcial Intelligence (AI) The ﬁeld of computer science focuses on creating 
machines that can perform tasks requiring human-like intelligence, such as learning, 
problem-solving, and decision-making. AI systems use data processing and pattern 
recognition to mimic cognitive functions. 
Beacon Technology Small wireless transmitters that send signals to nearby mobile 
devices, used in libraries to provide location-based information and services to users. 

Glossary 431 
Big Data Analytics The process of examining large and complex data sets to 
uncover patterns and insights, used in libraries to improve decision-making and 
enhance user services. 
Blockchain Technology A decentralized, secure digital ledger system that can be 
used in libraries for managing digital rights, tracking provenance of materials, and 
enhancing data security. 
Big Data Extremely large data sets can be analyzed computationally to reveal pat-
terns, trends, and associations. 
Blockchain Technology A decentralized digital ledger that records transactions 
across many computers so that the record cannot be altered retroactively. 
Cataloging The process of creating and organizing metadata for library resources 
to facilitate discovery and access. Modern cataloging often incorporates AI-assisted 
tools. 
Change Management Strategies and processes used to guide libraries through 
organizational transitions, such as implementing new technologies or restructuring 
services. 
Civic Engagement Libraries’ efforts to promote community involvement in public 
issues, often through programming, information provision, and collaborative spaces. 
Cloud-Based Services Library systems and resources hosted on remote servers, 
allowing for scalable, accessible, and cost-effective digital services. 
Coding Workshops Educational programs offered by libraries to teach program-
ming skills, often as part of digital literacy initiatives. 
Collaboration Partnerships between libraries and other institutions or community 
groups to enhance services, share resources, and achieve common goals. 
Collaborative Learning Educational approaches that encourage interaction and 
knowledge sharing among library users, often facilitated by library spaces and tech-
nologies. 
Collaborative Workspaces Areas within libraries designed to support group work, 
featuring shared technology and ﬂexible furniture arrangements. 
Collection Development The process of selecting, acquiring, and managing library 
materials to meet the needs and interests of the community served. 
Community Dialogue Libraries’ role in facilitating discussions on local issues and 
fostering communication between diverse community groups. 
Community Engagement Libraries’ efforts to interact with and involve local com-
munities in library services, programs, and decision-making processes. 
Community Gathering Spots Libraries serving as social hubs where people can 
meet, interact, and participate in various activities beyond traditional library services. 
Community Hubs Libraries functioning as central locations for community activ-
ities, information access, and social interaction. 

432 Glossary 
Community Outreach Programs and services designed to extend library resources 
and beneﬁts to underserved or hard-to-reach populations. 
Community Technology Hubs Libraries providing access to advanced technolo-
gies like 3D printers, VR equipment, and coding resources for community use and 
learning. 
Continuous Improvement The ongoing effort to enhance library services, pro-
cesses, and user experiences through regular evaluation and adaptation. 
Continuous Learning and Adaptation Libraries’ commitment to staying current 
with evolving technologies, user needs, and best practices through ongoing staff 
development and service reﬁnement. 
Copyright Challenges Legal and ethical issues faced by libraries in balancing 
access to information with respect for intellectual property rights in the digital age. 
Cultural Preservation Libraries’ role in safeguarding and providing access to 
materials of cultural signiﬁcance, often through digitization and special collections. 
Custodians of Knowledge Libraries’ traditional role as institutions responsible for 
collecting, preserving, and providing access to diverse forms of information and 
cultural heritage. 
Clay Tablets Early writing medium used in ancient Mesopotamia, made from wet 
clay and inscribed with cuneiform script. 
Callimachus A Greek poet and scholar who created one of the ﬁrst comprehensive 
library catalogs at the Library of Alexandria. 
Custodian of Knowledge The traditional role of libraries in preserving and pro-
viding access to knowledge. 
Community Hub The evolving role of libraries as centers for community engage-
ment, lifelong learning, and social interaction. 
Cloud-Based Infrastructure Computing services provided over the internet (the 
cloud), including storage, processing, and software. 
Collaborative Preservation Networks Groups of organizations work together to 
preserve digital content and ensure its long-term accessibility. 
Conversational AI The use of artiﬁcial intelligence to enable machines to interact 
with humans in a natural, conversational manner. 
Computer Vision A ﬁeld of AI that enables computers to interpret and make deci-
sions based on visual data from the world. 
Data Analytics The use of statistical and computational techniques to analyze 
library data, informing decision-making and service improvements. 
Data Integration The process of combining data from various library systems and 
sources to create a uniﬁed view, enhancing analysis and service delivery. 
Data Privacy Protecting users’ personal information and ensuring conﬁdentiality 
in library services, particularly important in digital environments. 

Glossary 433 
Data Processing The collection, manipulation, and analysis of data in library sys-
tems to support operations, decision-making, and user services. 
Data Visualization Graphical representation of data to aid understanding and 
decision-making in library management and user services. 
Data-Driven Decision Making Using data analysis to inform library policies, 
resource allocation, and service development. 
Decision-Making Automation Employing AI and algorithms to automate routine 
decisions in library operations, such as collection management or resource allocation. 
Deep Learning Advanced machine learning techniques used in libraries for com-
plex tasks like natural language processing and image recognition. 
Deep Learning Applications Speciﬁc uses of deep learning in libraries, such as 
automated indexing, content recommendation, or chatbot interactions. 
Digital Accessibility Ensuring that digital library resources and services are usable 
by people with disabilities, often through adaptive technologies and universal design 
principles. 
Digital Age Adaptations Changes in library services, spaces, and policies to meet 
the evolving needs of users in an increasingly digital world. 
Digital Archives Collections of digitized or born-digital materials preserved and 
made accessible by libraries for long-term use and research. 
Digital Assistant AI-powered tools that help library users navigate resources, 
answer questions, and provide personalized recommendations. 
Digital Collections Online repositories of digitized or born-digital materials curated 
and made accessible by libraries. 
Digital Collections Evolution The ongoing development and adaptation of digital 
library collections to meet changing user needs and technological capabilities. 
Digital Connectivity Providing internet access and digital resources to library 
users, bridging the digital divide in communities. 
Digital Divide The gap between those who have ready access to digital technologies 
and those who do not, which libraries strive to address through their services. 
Digital Exhibition Spaces Online platforms used by libraries to showcase collec-
tions, curate thematic displays, and engage users with digital content. 
Digital Formats Integration The incorporation of various digital media types (e.g., 
e-books, audiobooks, streaming video) into library collections and services. 
Digital Lending The practice of loaning e-books, audiobooks, and other digital 
materials to library users through online platforms. 
Digital Literacy The ability to use digital technologies effectively, which libraries 
promote through training programs and resources. 

434 Glossary 
Digital Literacy Development Libraries’ efforts to improve users’ skills in navi-
gating, evaluating, and creating digital content through workshops, resources, and 
hands-on experiences. 
Digital Literacy Programs Structured educational initiatives offered by libraries 
to enhance users’ digital skills and competencies. 
Digital Navigational Tools Software and interfaces designed to help users efﬁ-
ciently search and browse digital library collections and resources. 
Digital Preservation Strategies and technologies used by libraries to ensure long-
term access to digital materials, protecting against obsolescence and degradation. 
Digital Resources Online materials and tools provided by libraries, including e-
books, databases, and digital archives. 
Digital Revolution The profound impact of digital technologies on libraries, trans-
forming services, collections, and user interactions. 
Digital Rights Management Technologies and policies used to control access to 
and usage of digital library materials, balancing copyright protection with user needs. 
Digital Transformation The comprehensive integration of digital technologies into 
all areas of library operations and services, often leading to fundamental changes in 
how libraries function and deliver value. 
Digital Transformation Strategies Planned approaches for implementing and 
managing the shift towards digital technologies and services in libraries. 
Digitization Technologies Tools and processes used to convert physical materials 
into digital formats, enabling broader access and preservation. 
Diversity and Inclusion Libraries’ efforts to ensure their collections, services, and 
staff represent and serve diverse communities equitably. 
Document Summarization AI-powered techniques used to create concise sum-
maries of lengthy documents, aiding users in quickly grasping key information. 
Digital Archives Collections of digital objects that are preserved for long-term 
access and use. 
Digital Divide The gap between those with access to modern information and com-
munication technology and those without. 
Digital Equity Ensuring that all individuals and communities have the information 
technology capacity needed for full social participation. 
Digital Literacy The ability to effectively and critically navigate, evaluate, and 
create information using various digital technologies. 
Data Analytics The process of examining data sets to conclude the information 
they contain, increasingly with specialized systems and software. 
Data Governance The management of the availability, usability, integrity, and 
security of the data employed in an organization. 

Glossary 435 
Deep Learning (DL) A subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with 
many layers (hence “deep”) to model complex patterns in large data sets. 
Digital Transformation The integration of digital technology into all areas of a 
business or organization, fundamentally changing how it operates and delivers value 
to customers. 
Emerging Technologies New and rapidly developing technologies that libraries 
explore and implement to enhance services and user experiences. 
Environmental Sustainability Libraries’ initiatives to reduce their environmental 
impact and promote ecological awareness in their communities. 
Ethical AI Use The responsible implementation of AI technologies in libraries, 
considering issues of privacy, fairness, and transparency. 
Ethical Considerations Moral and professional principles guiding library deci-
sions and practices, especially in areas like privacy, access, and technology use. 
Ethical Data Use Responsible collection, storage, and application of user data in 
library services, respecting privacy and consent. 
Electronic Resource Management System (ERMS) Software used by libraries to 
manage the lifecycle of electronic resources such as e-journals and databases. 
Entity Recognition and Linking The process of identifying entities in text and 
linking them to a knowledge base. 
Ethical AI The branch of AI ensures that AI technologies are developed and used 
fairly, transparently, and accountable. 
Flexible Learning Environments Adaptable library spaces that can be reconﬁg-
ured to support various learning styles and activities. 
Future-Prooﬁng Library Design Creating library spaces and systems that can 
adapt to future technological and social changes without major overhauls. 
Gamiﬁed Experiences Incorporating game-like elements into library services and 
programs to increase user engagement and learning outcomes. 
Gutenberg Printing Press An invention by Johannes Gutenberg in the 15th century 
that revolutionized the production of books and dissemination of knowledge. 
Graph Databases Databases that use graph structures for semantic queries, with 
nodes, edges, and properties to represent and store data. 
Graph Query Languages (e.g., Cypher, SPARQL) Languages used to query 
graph databases and extract information from them. 
Graph Databases Databases that use graph structures for semantic queries, with 
nodes, edges, and properties to represent and store data. 
Hybrid Service Models Approaches that blend traditional in-person library ser-
vices with digital and remote offerings to meet diverse user needs. 

436 Glossary 
Impact Measurement Assessing and quantifying the effects of library services and 
programs on individuals and communities to demonstrate value and guide improve-
ments. 
Inclusive Communities Libraries’ efforts to create welcoming environments and 
services that accommodate diverse populations and needs. 
Inclusive Design Designing library spaces, services, and resources to be accessible 
and usable by people with a wide range of abilities and backgrounds. 
Information Navigation Guiding users through complex information landscapes, 
helping them ﬁnd and evaluate relevant resources efﬁciently. 
Information Retrieval The process of locating and accessing speciﬁc information 
within library collections, often aided by advanced search technologies. 
Innovation Culture Fostering an organizational environment that encourages cre-
ative problem-solving and the exploration of new ideas in library services. 
Innovative Management Leadership approaches that promote creativity, adapt-
ability, and forward-thinking in library operations and services. 
Intelligent Automation The use of AI and machine learning to automate complex 
library tasks that require decision-making capabilities. 
Interactive Experiences Engaging library programs and services that encourage 
active participation and hands-on learning from users. 
Interactive Learning Educational approaches in libraries that promote active 
engagement with information and resources, often through technology-enhanced 
experiences. 
Internet of Things The network of connected devices used in libraries to enhance 
services, such as smart shelves or automated environmental controls. 
Inventory Management Systems and processes for tracking and organizing library 
materials, often utilizing RFID technology or AI-assisted tools. 
Interdisciplinary Research Research involves integrating and synthesizing ideas 
and methods from different disciplines. 
Integrated Library System (ILS) An enterprise resource planning system for a 
library used to track items owned, orders made, bills paid, and patrons who have 
borrowed. 
Internet of Things (IoT) The network of physical objects embedded with sensors, 
software, and other technologies to connect and exchange data with other devices 
and systems over the internet. 
Knowledge Democratization Libraries’ role in making information freely and 
equally accessible to all members of society. 
Knowledge Management Strategies for effectively organizing, storing, and shar-
ing information within library systems and among staff. 

Glossary 437 
Knowledge Preservation Libraries’ efforts to safeguard information and cultural 
heritage for future generations, through both physical and digital means. 
Knowledge Representation and Reasoning AI technique represents information 
about the world in a form that a computer system can utilize to solve complex tasks 
such as diagnosing a medical condition or having a dialogue in natural language. 
Knowledge Graphs Structured representations of information that capture the rela-
tionships between entities and concepts. 
Library Management The overall administration and coordination of library 
resources, staff, and services to meet organizational goals and user needs. 
Library Services Enhancement Continuous improvement of library offerings 
through technology integration, user feedback, and innovative approaches. 
Library Transformation The ongoing process of adapting library spaces, services, 
and roles to meet evolving community needs and technological advancements. 
Lifelong Learning Libraries’ support for continuous education and skill develop-
ment throughout users’ lives through resources, programs, and services. 
Library of Alexandria One of the ancient world’s largest and most signiﬁcant 
libraries, located in Alexandria, Egypt. 
Lifelong Learning The ongoing, voluntary, and self-motivated pursuit of knowl-
edge for personal or professional reasons. 
Machine Learning AI techniques that enable computer systems to improve their 
performance on tasks through experience, used in various library applications. 
Misinformation Combat Libraries’ efforts to promote information literacy and 
provide reliable sources to counter the spread of false or misleading information. 
Mixed Reality Technologies blending physical and digital environments, used in 
libraries for interactive learning experiences and innovative service delivery. 
Mobile Access Providing library services and resources optimized for smartphones 
and tablets, allowing users to access information on-the-go. 
Monastic and Medieval Libraries Historical institutions that preserved knowl-
edge during the Middle Ages, often associated with religious orders and manuscripts. 
MOOC Hubs Libraries serving as access points and support centers for Massive 
Open Online Courses, facilitating digital learning opportunities. 
Multifunctional Areas Flexible library spaces designed to accommodate various 
activities, from quiet study to collaborative work and community events. 
Mobile-First Design A design philosophy that starts the design process with mobile 
devices in mind and then expands to larger screens. 
Monastic Libraries Libraries located within monasteries that preserved and copied 
religious and classical texts during the Middle Ages. 
Makerspaces Collaborative workspaces in libraries where people can gather to 
create, invent, and learn using various tools and technologies. 

438 Glossary 
Machine Learning (ML) A subset of AI that uses algorithms and statistical models 
to enable computers to improve their performance on tasks through experience. 
Machine Learning (ML) A subset of AI that uses algorithms and statistical models 
to enable computers to improve their performance on tasks through experience. 
Natural Language Processing AI technology that enables computers to under-
stand, interpret, and generate human language, used in library chatbots and search 
systems. 
Natural Language Processing (NLP) A ﬁeld of AI that focuses on the interac-
tion between computers and human languages, enabling computers to understand, 
interpret, and generate human language. 
Named Entity Recognition (NER) An NLP technique used to identify and clas-
sify named entities in text into predeﬁned categories such as the names of persons, 
organizations, and locations. 
Natural Language Processing (NLP) A ﬁeld of AI that focuses on the interac-
tion between computers and human languages, enabling computers to understand, 
interpret, and generate human language. 
Online Databases Digital collections of organized information provided by 
libraries, offering users access to scholarly articles, research papers, and other 
resources. 
Open Access Initiatives Efforts to make research and scholarly publications freely 
available online, often supported and promoted by libraries. 
Pandemic Response Libraries’ adaptations to continue providing services during 
health crises, including enhanced digital offerings and safety measures. 
Participatory Design Involving library users and community members in the plan-
ning and development of library spaces, services, and programs. 
Personalization Tailoring library services and recommendations to individual user 
preferences and needs, often through AI-driven systems. 
Personalized Services Customized library offerings based on user preferences, 
behavior, and needs, often enabled by data analytics and AI. 
Phygital Experiences Blending physical and digital elements in library services 
and spaces to create seamless, integrated user experiences. 
Predictive Analytics Using data, statistical algorithms, and machine learning tech-
niques to identify the likelihood of future outcomes in library operations. 
Predictive Modeling Creating statistical models to forecast future trends and behav-
iors in library usage and resource needs. 
Privacy and Ethics Considerations and practices ensuring the protection of user 
data and adherence to ethical standards in library operations. 
Privacy and Security in Design Incorporating data protection and user privacy 
considerations into the development of library systems and services from the outset. 

Glossary 439 
Privacy Concerns Issues related to the collection, storage, and use of user data in 
library systems, particularly in the context of digital services. 
Professional Values Core principles guiding librarians’ work, including intellec-
tual freedom, privacy, equity of access, and lifelong learning. 
Public Libraries Community-centered institutions providing free access to infor-
mation, resources, and services to the general public. 
Public Lending The practice of libraries lending books and other materials to the 
public for a speciﬁed period. 
Predictive Analytics The use of statistical techniques and algorithms to analyze 
historical data and make predictions about future events. 
Participatory Design An approach to design that involves all stakeholders (e.g., 
employees, partners, customers, citizens, end-users) in the design process to help 
ensure the result meets their needs. 
Recommendation Systems AI-powered tools that suggest relevant resources to 
users based on their preferences, behavior, and similar users’ activities. 
Redeﬁning Library Spaces The ongoing process of reimagining and redesigning 
physical library environments to meet changing user needs and expectations. 
Reimagining Physical Spaces Redesigning library layouts and furnishings to 
accommodate new technologies, collaborative work, and diverse community needs. 
Reliable Information Accurate, trustworthy, and authoritative resources that 
libraries curate and provide access to, countering misinformation. 
Reliable Information Dissemination Libraries’ role in providing and promoting 
accurate, trustworthy information to their communities. 
Remote Access Capabilities Technologies and systems allowing users to access 
library resources and services from off-site locations. 
Remote Learning Support Library services and resources designed to assist users 
engaged in distance education or online learning programs. 
Renaissance Libraries Historical institutions that ﬂourished during the Renais-
sance period, often associated with the revival of classical learning and humanism. 
Resource Management The efﬁcient allocation and use of library materials, staff, 
and facilities to meet user needs and organizational goals. 
Resource Sharing Collaboration between libraries to expand access to materials 
and services, often through interlibrary loan systems. 
Recommendation Systems Algorithms designed to suggest items to users based 
on various factors such as user preferences and behavior. 
Resource Description Framework (RDF) A standard model for data interchange 
on the web, which uses triples consisting of a subject, predicate, and object. 
Scholarship Support Library services and resources designed to assist researchers, 
academics, and students in their scholarly pursuits. 

440 Glossary 
Semantic Analysis AI-powered techniques for understanding the meaning and con-
text of text, used in advanced library search and recommendation systems. 
Service Enhancement Continuous improvement of library offerings through tech-
nology integration, user feedback, and innovative approaches. 
Service Optimization Reﬁning library services to maximize efﬁciency, effective-
ness, and user satisfaction, often through data analysis and user feedback. 
Smart Building Technologies Integration of IoT devices and AI systems in library 
facilities to improve energy efﬁciency, safety, and user comfort. 
Smart Digital Libraries Advanced library systems that use AI, IoT, and data ana-
lytics to provide personalized, efﬁcient, and adaptive services to users. 
Smart Library Spaces Physical library environments enhanced with technology 
to improve user experiences, resource management, and space utilization. 
Smart Shelves Library shelving systems equipped with RFID or other technologies 
to track item locations and assist with inventory management. 
Societal Challenges Broader issues that libraries address through their services, 
such as digital divide, information literacy, and community engagement. 
Societal Changes Shifts in demographics, technology use, and information needs 
that libraries adapt to in order to remain relevant and effective. 
Space Utilization Analytics Data-driven analysis of how library spaces are used, 
informing design decisions and resource allocation. 
Staff Development Ongoing training and skill enhancement for library personnel 
to keep pace with technological advancements and changing user needs. 
Stakeholder Engagement Involving various groups (users, community leaders, 
partners) in library decision-making and development processes. 
Strategic Planning Long-term visioning and goal-setting processes that guide 
library development and resource allocation. 
System Design The process of creating and implementing efﬁcient, user-friendly 
library management systems and digital platforms. 
Semantic Search Search techniques that improve search accuracy by understand-
ing the contextual meaning of terms as they appear in the searchable data space. 
Technological Advancements Ongoing developments in computing, networking, 
and digital technologies that impact library services and operations. 
Technological Impacts The effects of new technologies on library services, user 
behavior, and information access patterns. 
Technology Integration The process of incorporating new digital tools and systems 
into existing library services and operations. 
Technology Reach The extent to which libraries provide access to and training for 
various technologies to their communities. 

Glossary 441 
Technology Workshops Educational programs offered by libraries to teach digital 
skills and familiarize users with new technologies. 
Technology-Enhanced Learning The use of digital tools and platforms to support 
and improve educational experiences in library settings. 
Theft Prevention Measures and technologies used to protect library materials from 
unauthorized removal or damage. 
Universal Design Creating library spaces, services, and resources that are accessi-
ble and usable by all people, regardless of age, ability, or other factors. 
User Behavior Analysis Studying how library patrons interact with resources and 
services to inform improvements and personalization. 
User Behavior Analytics The use of data analysis tools to understand patterns in 
how users interact with library resources and services. 
User Data Analytics Analyzing information about library users to improve ser-
vices, inform decision-making, and enhance user experiences. 
User Empowerment Providing tools, resources, and skills that enable library users 
to independently access and utilize information effectively. 
User Engagement Strategies and practices to actively involve library patrons in 
services, programs, and decision-making processes. 
User Experience Design Creating library interfaces, spaces, and services that are 
intuitive, efﬁcient, and satisfying for users. 
User Interface Customization Allowing users to personalize their digital library 
interfaces to suit their preferences and needs. 
User Personalization Tailoring library services, recommendations, and experi-
ences to individual user preferences and behaviors. 
User Privacy and Data Security Measures taken to protect user information and 
ensure conﬁdentiality in library systems and services. 
User-Centered Design Designing library services and spaces based on an under-
standing of user needs, preferences, and behaviors. 
User-Centric Design An approach to library service and space design that priori-
tizes user needs and experiences. 
User-Centric Space Design Creating library environments that are tailored to meet 
the diverse needs and preferences of the user community. 
User-Centered Design An iterative design process in which designers focus on the 
users and their needs in each phase of the design process. 
Virtual and Physical Integration Blending digital services with physical library 
spaces to create seamless user experiences. 
Virtual Reality Immersive technology used in libraries for educational experi-
ences, virtual tours, and innovative service delivery. 

442 Glossary 
Virtual Reference Services Online platforms and tools that allow librarians to 
assist users remotely with research and information needs. 
Virtual Reality (VR) A simulated experience similar to or completely different 
from the real world, typically involving immersive visual and auditory experiences. 
Voice-Activated Technology Technology allows users to interact with devices 
through voice commands. 
Workforce Development Library programs and resources aimed at supporting job 
seekers, career changers, and skills development in the community.
